title: Fleet Control Panel: scaling presets, SLA-backed throughput targets, and activity timeline
creator: Ariana Park
description:
Problem: Platform customers running Redwood Dedicated need a single place in the Console to manage fleet-level scaling behavior, define throughput guarantees associated with reserved capacity, and inspect chronological changes to scaling and routing policies. Current controls are spread across the Autoscale Workbench, Fleet Manager, and runtime config pages, causing confusion during on-call and pre-launch tuning.

Objective: Build a Fleet Control Panel inside the Console that consolidates: 1) scaling presets (manual, adaptive, target-throughput), 2) SLA-backed throughput target configuration that maps to reserved capacity and fallbacks, and 3) an activity timeline showing who changed what, when, and why (with links to related PRs, runbooks, and incident notes). The panel should make it simple for platform engineers to set predictable throughput guarantees while seeing historical context for changes.

Scope: UI for presets + target throughput configuration, backend API surfaces for saving presets and recording audit entries, telemetry capture for throughput backfills and effective capacity, server-side validation to ensure preset combos are compatible with customer's Dedicated contract. Excludes on-prem install flows (tracked separately) and autoscaler engine algorithm changes (will integrate with existing autoscale service via API).

Success metrics: 
- Reduced time-to-configure a new fleet scaling policy from 35m → <10m for common recipes.
- 90% of Dedicated customers onboards use presets within first 2 weeks of Console GA.
- Mean time to root-cause for scaling regressions down by 25% due to visible history and links.

User personas: Platform engineer (primary), SRE/On-call (secondary), Customer success (supporting), Solutions engineer (pre-sales demos).
acceptance_criteria: Fleet Control Panel accessible from Fleet Overview with role-based access
Create/edit/delete scaling presets with validation and preview of expected throughput/latency impact
Define SLA-backed throughput target that ties to reserved GPU pools and shows estimated cost delta
Activity timeline shows chronological entries: change summary, actor, timestamp, link to related PR or runbook
Audit entries are immutable and exportable as CSV
API endpoints documented and available for programmatic preset management
Telemetry emitted for each change event and preset application (events: preset_created, preset_applied, preset_reverted, target_updated)
E2E tests cover UI flows and backend persistence; integration tests verify autoscaler receives updates
technical_notes: Backend: extend /api/fleets/:id/presets to support named presets + JSON schema versioning
Audit: use existing audit-log service; append structured metadata (actor_id, ip, before/after) and store pointer to PR/runbook
Validation: server-side check against customer's capacity contract (reserved_gpus, max_burst) before accepting SLA targets
Telemetry: add metrics for preset adoption, preset application success/failure, and delta between target throughput and observed throughput
UI: new Fleet Control Panel React view under /fleets/:id/control; reuse existing pattern library components for forms and timeline entries
Security: changes to presets should be limited by RBAC role fleet-admin; write unit tests for permission gating
Backward compatibility: existing autoscale webhooks still honored; new presets are additive and can be applied incrementally
dependencies: ENG-6301 (extend autoscale API to accept preset payload)
ENG-6715 (audit-log indexing improvements for activity timeline)
DES-212 (control panel visual design and accessibility review)
PM-8922 (pricing calc for SLA-backed throughput to show cost delta)

Each phase gated by adoption and telemetry thresholds. Communication: release notes, in-console guided tour, and dedicated webinar for platform customers.
